question: Why is backpropagation often described as reverse-mode automatic differentiation?
direct_answer: Because it computes derivatives of one scalar output with respect to many inputs by propagating sensitivities backward through a computation graph.
expanded_answer: In neural network training, the loss is usually a single scalar, while the model has many parameters. Reverse-mode autodiff is ideal for this setting because it efficiently computes gradients of that scalar with respect to many variables in one backward sweep, which is exactly what backprop does.
common_wrong_ideas: Reverse-mode means the network runs backward at inference time
Automatic differentiation is the same as numerical finite differences
Backprop only applies to fully connected layers
